questions.question: How do I create a new project?
questions.answer: Project creation is reserved to the platform's superadministration (a deliberate anti-abuse measure). If you need a new project, contact the platform team; they create it and designate you as its administrator.

questions.question: In what order do I set up a new project?
questions.answer: The natural order: 1) define the unit types; 2) load each type's units; 3) optionally build the plan; 4) create the families (each with its type) and invite at least one member of each; 5) publish any events you need and agree on the lottery date. Creation of all of these lives in the + (Quick Actions) button, top right.

questions.question: Do I have to load every member of every family?
questions.answer: No: invite at least one per family. Each member can invite the rest of their own family, and each invitee completes their registration from the emailed link.

questions.question: How do I schedule the lottery?
questions.answer: The lottery event is created automatically with the project — you don't create it and can't delete it. Edit it to set or change its date and description; this is possible while the lottery hasn't been executed.

questions.question: When can I run the lottery?
questions.answer: When all families are registered with their correct type and all units are loaded. Families can register and modify preferences until the moment of execution; when you run it, they lock automatically.

questions.question: What if the number of families and units doesn't match?
questions.answer: The system detects it, warns you and asks for your confirmation before continuing. If you confirm, the lottery runs taking the imbalance into account.

questions.question: The execution failed, what do I do?
questions.answer: Nothing is lost: the lottery returns to its previous state (preferences unlock), the error is recorded in the audit log, and you can retry whenever you want.

questions.question: Can I undo an executed lottery?
questions.answer: No — the result is final by design. Only in exceptional situations (e.g. a data error discovered afterwards) can the superadministration invalidate the whole execution, leaving an audit record, so the data can be fixed and the lottery run again.

questions.question: Can I see the families' preferences?
questions.answer: No: preferences are private to each family. You see the overall state of the process and, after execution, the result and its audit log.

questions.question: Can I manage several projects?
questions.answer: Yes, without limit. The application works on one selected project at a time; you switch it from the Projects section.

questions.question: I deleted a family (or a member) by mistake
questions.answer: It's not catastrophic: families, members and shared content can be restored. No data is lost.

questions.question: What is recorded for each lottery?
questions.answer: Everything: who ran it, with which families, units and preferences (frozen at execution time), the result of each per-type sub-lottery, and any failure or invalidation. That audit record is permanent and makes the result verifiable.
